question: What is the main sign of a food fad?

options.A: It is a lifelong medical diet prescribed by a qualified physician.
options.B: It is a government-regulated nutrition program for school children.
options.C: It is a traditional cultural meal plan passed down for generations.
options.D: It is an intense and short-lived dietary trend without scientific backing.

explanation: Food fads come and go very quickly. They usually make big health claims that have zero real science behind them. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h1)

question: Why do people easily fall for popular food trends?

options.A: Scientific journals publish strict guidelines endorsing them.
options.B: These trends offer appealing quick fixes for body image and wellness goals.
options.C: Hospitals and clinics mandate these diets for all new admissions.
options.D: Nutritional fads are always cheaper than buying regular food items.

explanation: Everyone loves a shortcut! When a diet promises fast, easy results, it's hard not to listen. Great job thinking it through. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h1)

question: How does social media help spread harmful diet trends?

options.A: It forces government agencies to approve new superfoods daily.
options.B: It lowers the market cost of rare and exotic dietary supplements.
options.C: It creates virtual communities that make strict rules feel rewarding.
options.D: It provides rigorous peer-reviewed data from medical doctors.

explanation: Online groups make people feel like they belong to a special team when they follow harsh diet rules together. Keep up the great study flow! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h2)

question: What usually pushes someone to start a very strict food fad?

options.A: An innate biological need to consume fewer than five hundred calories
options.B: A clinical requirement to study human metabolism in real-time
options.C: A professional obligation to test new commercial food products
options.D: A desire for control and quick solutions to personal anxieties

explanation: When life feels overwhelming, people often use strict food rules to regain a sense of personal control. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h2)

question: Which of these is a major warning sign of fake nutrition advice?

options.A: Advising patients to eat a balanced variety of all food groups
options.B: Publishing raw data from randomized and controlled clinical trials
options.C: Requiring regular blood tests supervised by a registered dietitian
options.D: Promising a single product can cure many different diseases

explanation: If one simple tea or supplement claims to cure everything from malaria to headaches, run the other way! Real medicine doesn't work that way. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h3)

question: Why should a nurse worry if a patient completely cuts out a major food group?

options.A: It usually lacks essential nutrients required for normal bodily functions.
options.B: It permanently damages the digestive tract within twenty-four hours.
options.C: It always costs significantly more money than cooking regular meals.
options.D: It is strictly illegal under international public health laws.

explanation: Our bodies need a mix of everything—carbs, proteins, fats. Dropping a whole food group usually leads to vitamin shortages. Well spotted! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h3)

question: Why do people lose weight so fast in the first few days of a strict fad diet?

options.A: Instantaneous healing of the gastrointestinal lining
options.B: Permanent destruction of abnormal fat cells in the abdomen
options.C: Loss of body water and breakdown of stored muscle protein
options.D: Rapid increase in physical activity levels induced by supplements

explanation: That quick drop on the scale isn't fat—it's mostly water weight and muscle glycogen being used up. Good to know as a future nurse! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h4)

question: A patient on a harsh detox diet feels dizzy, weak, and has muscle cramps. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Sudden overproduction of essential vitamins in the liver
options.B: Rapid cleansing of toxins from the central nervous system
options.C: Electrolyte imbalances and severe caloric depletion
options.D: Increased metabolic efficiency burning excess fat stores

explanation: Starving the body of proper food and water messes up vital minerals (electrolytes) like sodium and potassium, causing weakness and cramps. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women especially at risk if they try fad diets?

options.A: Hormonal shifts make them immune to the marketing of superfoods.
options.B: They have increased nutrient needs for fetal development that fads fail to meet.
options.C: Their digestive systems cannot process any foods except simple sugars.
options.D: Medical insurance never covers nutritional counseling for expectant mothers.

explanation: Pregnancy requires extra nutrients for the growing baby. Restrictive diets can easily starve the baby of what it needs to form properly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h5)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out if a patient is trying a risky diet?

options.A: Scolding the patient immediately for reading health advice online
options.B: Asking open-ended questions about how the patient manages their weight
options.C: Threatening to report the use of herbal supplements to the hospital board
options.D: Refusing to provide medical care until the patient stops buying vitamins

explanation: Patients won't open up if you judge them. Friendly, open-ended questions make them feel safe to tell the truth. You're going to be a great nurse! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h6)

question: A patient proudly tells you they stopped eating all carbs and dairy to lose weight fast. What is your next best step as a nurse?

options.A: Immediately prescribe a high-calorie hospital diet to reverse the weight loss
options.B: Congratulate the patient on achieving rapid weight loss without any concern
options.C: Assess for nutrient deficiencies and discuss the health risks of restrictive eating
options.D: Tell the patient to stop visiting the clinic until they reach their target goal

explanation: Always educate gently! Check their nutritional health and calmly explain why cutting out entire food groups can hurt them in the long run. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h6)

question: What is the main goal of nutrition counseling given by a nurse?

options.A: To sell government-approved dietary supplements directly from the clinic
options.B: To force the patient to follow a rigid hospital-approved meal plan forever
options.C: To convince the patient that all commercial vitamins are completely toxic
options.D: To guide the patient toward sustainable and balanced eating habits

explanation: Good nursing isn't about temporary fixes; it's about helping patients build healthy eating habits they can actually maintain for life. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h7)

question: Which professional is best suited to work with a nurse in creating a specialized meal plan for a patient?
explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Registered dietitians are the absolute experts when it comes to planning safe, personalized diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h7)
